introduction.text: The Chiesa di Santa Maria in Scala Coeli is a Roman Catholic church in Rome, part of the Tre Fontane Abbey complex, notable for its historical association with St Paul the Apostle's imprisonment and its architectural and devotional significance.

history.description: In 1500, Henry VII of England was granted the scala coeli indulgence for his new chapel in Westminster Abbey.
By the 1520s, bequests for masses at Scala Coeli were common.
The ancient church was refurbished in 1582 by Vignola under the patronage of Cardinal Alessandro Farnese.
Pope John Paul II officially granted the church to the Romanian Orthodox community in 2002.
The present church was designed by Giacomo della Porta under the patronage of Cardinal Pietro Aldobrandini.
The location of the church is held by tradition to be where St Paul the Apostle was imprisoned.

design.description: The interior layout of the church is octagonal.
Stairs leading to the church have writings and drawings scratched into the stone, likely instructions from the architect to the builders.

art.description: The presbytery contains a mosaic by Francesco Zucca based on designs by Giovanni della Vecchia.
